text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans, Minister of Education and Science Juris Celmins and Minister of Agriculture Roberts Dilba reject allegations they have violated the anti-corruption law.
- On Saturday criminals robbed 22 tourists on an Italian-bound bus to Italy 32 kilometers from Riga.
- The Swedish Royal Navy and Latvian Naval forces detected and eliminated five mines during a joint-exercise. There are about 13,000 mines in the Gulf of Riga.

- Today the parliamentary faction of Fatherland and Freedom wants to meet Prime Minister Andris Shkele to head off the impending government crisis. The chairman of Fatherland and Freedom's parliamentary faction, Janis Straume, said the party will leave government if Shkele asks for the resignation of Economics Minister Guntars Krasts.
- The port of Ventspils celebrates its 100th anniversary.
